meta.title: Self-Hosted TTS Servers
meta.tagline: OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech you run on your own hardware
meta.intro: A curated index of text-to-speech you can host yourself: HTTP servers that expose an OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint, the local inference engines underneath them, voice-cloning backends, browser UIs, and long-form generators. Every entry links to the upstream project; nothing here is a re-host or a mirror.
meta.disclaimer: Compiled from public sources — no independent testing of the linked projects. Star counts were read from the GitHub API on 2026-10-16 and drift daily.

sections.title: OpenAI-compatible servers
sections.description: Drop-in replacements for the OpenAI speech endpoint. Point an existing client at these instead of api.openai.com and nothing else in your stack has to change.

items.name: Kokoro-FastAPI
items.what: Dockerized FastAPI wrapper around Kokoro-82M exposing an OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint, with voice mixing and multiple output formats. The most-starred dedicated TTS server here.

items.name: Chatterbox-TTS-Server
items.what: Self-hosting front end for the Chatterbox model, shipping both a web UI for auditioning voices and an API surface for programmatic use.

items.name: chatterbox-tts-api
items.what: A deliberately minimal local OpenAI-compatible TTS API built on Chatterbox, aimed at people who want the endpoint and not much else.

items.name: openedai-speech
items.what: OpenAI-API-compatible server over Coqui xtts_v2 with voice cloning. Archived upstream — listed because it is still widely forked and referenced, not because it is maintained.

items.name: xtts-api-server
items.what: A simple FastAPI server for XTTSv2 covering voice cloning, multiple languages and streaming responses.

items.name: Chatterbox-TTS-Extended
items.what: Fork of Chatterbox that accepts whole text files as input and batches long-form synthesis rather than one utterance at a time.

items.name: Dia-TTS-Server
items.what: Serving wrapper for the Dia model, focused on multi-speaker dialogue rather than single-narrator speech.

items.name: mlx-omni-server
items.what: Local inference server built on Apple's MLX, exposing OpenAI-shaped endpoints for speech and other modalities on Apple Silicon.

sections.title: Inference engines
sections.description: The model runtimes the servers above are thin wrappers around. Useful directly when you want to embed synthesis in-process instead of over HTTP.

items.name: Coqui TTS
items.what: The long-standing deep-learning TTS toolkit. The original company shut down and the repo is archived; the community continuation is the next entry.

items.name: coqui-ai-TTS (community fork)
items.what: Maintained fork of Coqui TTS under the Idiap research institute, keeping XTTS and the rest of the toolkit installable on current Python.

items.name: F5-TTS
items.what: Flow-matching TTS trained to clone a voice from a short reference clip, with an actively developed training and inference codebase.

items.name: Orpheus-TTS
items.what: Llama-based speech model producing expressive output with paralinguistic tags such as laughter and sighs.

items.name: Kokoro
items.what: An 82M-parameter open-weight TTS model that punches well above its size, and the reason most of the servers above exist.

items.name: kokoro-onnx
items.what: Kokoro reimplemented on ONNX Runtime, trading the PyTorch dependency for a portable inference graph.

items.name: Piper
items.what: Fast local neural TTS designed for Raspberry Pi-class hardware. Archived at this path; development continues in the GPL fork below.

items.name: piper1-gpl
items.what: The current home of Piper development, relicensed and restructured with a C API and Python bindings.

items.name: sherpa-onnx
items.what: ONNX-based speech toolkit spanning TTS, recognition and diarisation across many platforms, with prebuilt binaries and language bindings.

items.name: espeak-ng
items.what: The formant synthesiser that will not win a naturalness contest but runs anywhere, in almost any language, and is a common fallback backend for larger systems.

sections.title: Browser and desktop front ends
sections.description: Graphical ways to drive local models without writing a client.

items.name: TTS-WebUI
items.what: Gradio and React interface bundling a large set of local speech and audio models behind one control panel.

items.name: TTS-Audio-Suite
items.what: ComfyUI custom nodes for local multi-engine, multi-language speech generation, for people already working inside a ComfyUI graph.

items.name: voice-pro
items.what: Gradio WebUI aimed at creators, combining TTS, voice cloning, translation and dubbing in one interface.

items.name: orpheus-tts-local
items.what: Runs the Orpheus 3B model locally through LM Studio, with a small client for driving it.

sections.title: Long-form generation
sections.description: Tooling that turns documents into hours of audio, where the hard part is chunking and pacing rather than the synthesis itself.

items.name: audiblez
items.what: Generates audiobooks from e-books, handling chapter detection and long-run synthesis locally.

items.name: abogen
items.what: Converts EPUBs, PDFs and plain text into audiobooks with synchronised captions and chapter-level progress tracking.
